segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Excuse me. Can you help me? I was looking for the Main Hall.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Maybe I can, actually. I’m looking for the Main Hall, too. I think it’s in the Administration building. Are you a new student?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Yes, I am.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: I thought you looked as lost as me. I’m trying to find the admin building, too, so that I can register for my course. But I don’t seem to be having much luck.

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Well, look, according to this map of the campus here, you go straight up the steps, turn left and the building is on the right. OK, let’s see if we can find it.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, this looks right. Oh, yeah, it must be. Look, there are hundreds of other people here!

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: There must be at least 50 people in the queue — we’ll be here till gone 2 o’clock at this rate.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: And I’m starving!

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: So am I.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Actually, I was on my way to the canteen to get something for lunch. Why don’t I go to the canteen and buy something and you stay here and wait?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Good idea.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: What would you like? Pizza, sandwich, hot dog, fried rice. They do everything ...

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, something easy. Take away fried rice sounds good.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: OK, fried ...

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: No, on second thoughts, I’ll have a cheese and tomato sandwich.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Right one cheese and tomato — anything to drink?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Yeah, get me a coffee, would you?

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, hot coffee’s a bit hard to carry. What about a coke or an orange juice?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, um ... get me an orange juice, then. Look, here’s five dollars.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, take two dollars back, it shouldn’t cost me more than three dollars.

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Well, keep the five and we’ll sort it out later. Oh, and could you get me an apple as well?

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: OK. Back in a minute.

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, hello. I’m here to register for the First Year Law course.

segments.speaker: CLERK
segments.en: I’ll just have to fill out this form for our records. What’s your name?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Julia Perkins.

segments.speaker: CLERK
segments.en: Can you spell that for me?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Yeah, that’s J-U-L-I-A P-E-R-K-I-N-S.

segments.speaker: CLERK
segments.en: Address?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Flat 5, 15 Waratah Road, that’s W-A-R-A-T-A-H, Brisbane. and

segments.speaker: CLERK
segments.en: Brisbane ... And your telephone number?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: We haven’t got the phone on yet. We’ve only just moved in.

segments.speaker: CLERK
segments.en: OK, well can you let us have the number once the phone’s connected and I’ll make a note here to be advised. And the course?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: I beg your pardon?

segments.speaker: CLERK
segments.en: What course are you doing?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: First Year Law.

segments.speaker: CLERK
segments.en: Right. Well, you’ll have to go across to the Law Faculty and get this card stamped and then you come back here with it and pay your union fee.

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Thanks very much.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, there you are.

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: I thought you were never going to come back.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Sorry! The canteen was absolutely packed and I had to wait for ages. Then when I got to the front of the queue they had hardly any food left. So I had to get you a slice of pizza. I’m sorry.

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, that’s OK. I could eat anything, I’m so hungry.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: And there’s your bottle of orange juice and your apple. At least I managed that.

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Great. Thanks a lot.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh and here’s your $2 back.

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Don’t worry about it. Buy me a cup of coffee later!

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, alright then! So how’d you go?

segments.speaker: FEMALE STUDENT
segments.en: Well in order to register we’ve got to go to the Law Faculty and get this card stamped and then go back to the Admin building and pay the union fees. That means we’re registered. After that we have to go to the notice board to find out about lectures and then we have to put our names down for tutorial groups and go to the library to ...

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Great. Well first let’s sit down and have our lunch.
